stories.headline: Sensex falls over 20% in dollar terms in 2026 as weak sentiment, rupee drag returns
stories.title: Sensex falls over 20% in dollar terms in 2026 as weak sentiment, rupee drag returns
stories.summary: Mumbai: The benchmark Sensex has fallen more than 20% so far in 2026 in dollar terms, the steepest in 15 years, as the rupee's weakening has amplified losses for overseas investors. The Nifty has declined 18.6% in dollar terms, with both indices emerging as the second-biggest laggards among major global markets after Indonesia.In rupee terms, the Sensex has declined 14.9%, while Nifty has lost 13.1% so far this year.134576922Foreign investors track the performance of overseas markets in dollar terms as their portfolio returns are typically measured in the US currency. A weaker rupee reduces their returns when Indian investments are converted back into dollars."The rupee's depreciation has adversely impacted returns in dollar terms, but the main cause of poor year-to-date returns is driven by the weak sentiment towards Indian equities," said Pratik Gupta, managing director and CEO of Kotak Institutional Equities.Read more: D-Street stocks are breaking long-held supports as selloff deepensIndian stocks have fallen out of favour with foreign investors since end-September 2024 amid slowing earnings growth, a shift toward AI-fuelled markets such as South Korea and Taiwan, US tariffs and, more recently, the spike in oil prices following the West Asia war. The rupee has declined 6.4% so far this year.The last time both indices recorded a sharper decline was in 2011, when they fell nearly 36% each in dollar terms.Read more: Nifty sees worst September series in 25 years. What does October hold?Contrast with global peersThe contrast with several global markets has been stark. In the US, the S&P 500 has gained 12.2% so far in 2026, while the Nasdaq and Dow Jones have risen 15% and 7%, respectively.In Europe, meanwhile, the FTSE 100 has gained 6%, while the CAC 40 has declined 4% and the DAX has risen 0.8%.Asian markets have also largely outperformed Indian equities. Japan's Nikkei has gained 30%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng has declined 6% and China's Shenzhen index has risen 0.8%. Taiwan and South Korea's Kospi have gained 61% and 72%, respectively. Indonesia's Jakarta Composite and the Philippines index have declined 34% and 11%, respectively.The Sensex is in a bear market if measured in dollar terms, having fallen more than 20% so far in 2026. A decline of 20% or more is widely regarded as the threshold for a bear market.Saion Mukherjee, head of India equity research at Nomura, said the 20% decline itself should not be viewed as a definitive threshold for a bear market, but the correction could affect investor sentiment and fund flows."Is it like 20% is a bear market? You can call it in some definition, but no line says 15% or 20%," he said. "The bigger point is how this correction impacts investor sentiment and domestic flows."Cushioning FPI outflowsIn the past year, foreign portfolio outflows of over ₹2.17 lakh crore have been offset by strong domestic mutual fund inflows of ₹4.98 lakh crore, cushioning the market from a sharper drop."People have been coming in and supporting the market whenever there is a fall. Will they continue to do that?" said Mukherjee. "The amount of money that's coming into mutual funds as a percentage of financial savings has been at a pretty elevated level in the last four-five years. For incremental investors to come and keep supporting and put money would require the market to be a bit supportive. I think that's a challenge."The Sensex's dollar-denominated market capitalisation has declined by more than $372 billion so far in 2026, with 10 stocks accounting for around 80% of the erosion.Market cap erosionReliance Industries has seen the largest decline, with its market capitalisation falling by nearly $70 billion, followed by HDFC Bank and TCS, with declines of around $54 billion and $52 billion, respectively.Infosys and ITC have recorded market-cap erosion of around $32 billion and $22 billion, respectively, while Maruti Suzuki India and Bharti Airtel have each seen declines of around $19 billion. Hindustan Unilever and Mahindra & Mahindra have seen their market capitalisation fall by around $15 billion each.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Questions Inflated Medicine Prices, Seeks Uniform Pricing Cap
stories.title: Supreme Court Questions Inflated Medicine Prices, Seeks Uniform Pricing Cap
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned the huge disparity between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the price at which they are supplied to retailers, asking the Centre why a uniform margin cap could not be prescribed for pharmaceutical products.
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta raised particular concern over cancer medicines carrying an MRP of Rs 27,000 while their price to retailers (PTR) was around Rs 3,000.

The apex court also flagged the practice of corporate hospitals requiring patients to purchase medicines from their in-house pharmacies, observing that patients who procure medicines from outside may not be assured treatment.
"Corporate hospitals say you have to buy from our chemist.
If you bring it from outside, we are not assuring treatment.
If that patient is taking treatment under a government scheme, who reimburses?
The taxpayer pays.
Why not uniform criteria?" it asked.

The Justice Vikram Nath-led Bench further questioned the distinction between essential and non-essential medicines under the Drug Price Control Order (DPCO), asking why a uniform margin per cent could not be prescribed across pharmaceutical products covered by the Essential Commodities Act.

It also raised concerns over the impact of a large MRP-PTR gap on consumer trust, observing that a patient could even suspect a medicine to be spurious if a drug carrying an MRP of Rs 27,000 was offered by a chemist for around Rs 3,000.
"Suppose there is a medicine, the patient goes to the chemist; the chemist says MRP may be Rs 27,000, I will give it for Rs 3,000.
Will the patient think it is genuine?

stories.headline: Supreme Court allows forensic audit in Fortis case
stories.title: Supreme Court allows forensic audit in Fortis case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The bench also chided Daiichi for giving up its plea for forensic audit of the dissipation of shares in the two companies, which was a major window for the banks to argue that HC could not have passed the order for forensic audit when decree holder had given up that plea.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld a Delhi HC order directing forensic audit of dissipation of shares of Fortis Healthcare Ltd (FHL) and Fortis Healthcare Holdings Pvt Ltd (FHHPL) through 17 banks and financial institutions allegedly to frustrate execution of a decade-old Rs 5,300 crore foreign decree by Daiichi Sankyo against brothers Malvinder and Shivinder Singh.

Brushing aside a challenge to the forensic audit order of the HC by senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing on behalf of Yes Bank and Axis Bank, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified the forensic audit would not be a roving inquiry against the banks or FIIs but will focus on the transaction of shares of FHL and FHHPL.
Daiichi counsel.

Arvind Datar told the court that the foreign decree, upheld by SC, had not been implemented for a decade and the plea giving up forensic audit was made due to frustration over the long lapse of time in executing the decree in India.

In fact, Delhi HC judge Justice Subramonium Prasad started his Aug 31 judgement quoting an 1872 judgement of Fort William HC (Calcutta HC) which stated “the difficulty of a litigant in India begins when he has obtained a decree”.
Delhi HC had said in its judgment, “For the loans taken by the downstream entities of the judgment-debtors (Singh brothers and their companies), shares of FHL held by FHHPL were kept as security.

This court needs to ascertain whether these loans were part of a legitimate transaction for the genuine business or were they part of the fraud to dissipate the shareholding of FHHPL in FHL to defeat the decree.” While directing the forensic auditor to identify each dealing in shareholdings aimed at frustrating the decree, Justice Prasad had asked it to examine “the role of banks, and identify the loan facilities secured by FHL shares, the creation and variation of security, maintenance of security margins, operation of contractual top-up obligations, invocation and sale of pledged shares, release of security, and the outstanding liability corresponding to each transaction”.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear plea for CEC’s suspension, voiding SIR next week
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear plea for CEC’s suspension, voiding SIR next week
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh alleged that about 14 decisions were taken in the EC’s name despite objections recorded by the two other election commissioners, S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear next week a petition filed against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, seeking his suspension and a declaration that the CEC cannot take unilateral decisions on the Election Commission’s behalf.

The petition also sought that special intensive revision of electoral rolls and all actions, decisions, directions and consequential measures undertaken pursuant to the exercise be declared void ab initio (invalid) and without lawful authority.
The plea was mentioned by senior advocate Vikas Singh before CJI Surya Kant.

He sought a direction to the CEC to “show under what authority he has acted, and continues to act” as though he is individually entitled to exercise the collective decision-making power vested by Article 324 of the Constitution in the EC.
Significantly, CEC has asserted that all decisions regarding SIR were taken unanimously by all election commissioners.

stories.headline: Noel Tata hopes Tata Sons, RBI find common ground; says merger proposal can help avoid listing
stories.title: Noel Tata hopes Tata Sons, RBI find common ground; says merger proposal can help avoid listing
stories.summary: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata said the proposed restructuring would transform Tata Sons into a holding-plus-operating company while addressing regulatory concerns
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata hopes Tata Sons and the Reserve Bank of India will find common ground and reach a solution that helps the holding company avoid a listing.

Speaking at an event hosted by Republic TV on Tuesday, Tata said he would like Tata Sons to review and, if necessary, modify the Trusts’ restructuring proposal to keep the holding company out of RBI’s regulatory framework for the non-banking finance company upper-layer category.
“We would like Tata Sons to engage with RBI as we believe this is a solution which will help us avoid listing,” Tata said.
On Monday, Tata Trusts proposed merger of Tata Consulting Engineers and Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Private Limited with Tata Sons.
This would convert Tata Sons from a pure holding company into a holding-plus-operating company.
“This is something which is very common among holding companies in India.
I hope the RBI will engage with us on the subject.
We should be able to find some common ground and hopefully a solution which avoids us from listing,” Tata said.
The issue of listing Tata Sons shares has divided the company’s board and its main shareholder, Tata Trusts.
Tata opposes listing Tata Sons, as it would change the company’s character.
The group’s philanthropic mandate could also change, he said.

While its operating companies are meant to earn profit and deliver shareholder returns, Tata Sons also serves a different purpose: dividends from group companies fund its charities, with a focus on education and health.

stories.headline: J&K sanctions 586 sports infrastructure works worth Rs 182.75 cr in 2026-27
stories.title: J&K sanctions 586 sports infrastructure works worth Rs 182.75 cr in 2026-27
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 29: The Jammu and Kashmir government has sanctioned 586 sports infrastructure works involving an approved allocation of Rs 182.75 crore during the financial year 2026-27, even as only 90 works have been completed so far, the Youth Services and Sports Department has informed the Legislative Assembly. The information was provided by the Youth Services and Sports Minister in response to a question raised by MLA Tral Rafiq Ahmad Naik regarding the construction, upgradation, renovation and expansion of sports stadiums and major sports complexes across J&K. According to the reply, the department sanctioned 587 works worth Rs 155.40 crore during 2025-26. Of these, 338 works were taken up and 272 were completed, while works involving playgrounds, sports infrastructure, buildings and other complexes accounted for 273 completed works as per the department's classification. For 2026-27, the department has sanctioned 362 ongoing works with an approved allocation of Rs 87.17 crore and 224 new works worth Rs 95.57 crore. Against the total allocation of Rs 182.75 crore, Rs 24.38 crore has been utilised so far. Of the 586 works sanctioned this financial year, 90 have been completed, while 80 works have been completed under the category covering development/upgradation of playfields/playgrounds, creation of sports infrastructure and construction of buildings and complexes. The government said two major sports projects have been sanctioned or taken up for execution in the Tral constituency. During 2023-24, development of a playground at Bajwani Tral Pulwama, including two dugouts, two practice pitches, two grounds and a synthetic volleyball court, was sanctioned at an estimated cost of Rs 70 lakh. The work was allotted at a cost of Rs 50.70 lakh, against which Rs 49.30 lakh has been utilised. The department said the project has been physically completed. The project received Rs 35 lakh, Rs 41.95 lakh and Rs 9.35 lakh during 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 respectively, with utilisation of Rs 3.96 lakh, Rs 37.39 lakh and Rs 7.95 lakh. A second project for development of a playfield at Koil Shikargah was sanctioned during 2025-26 at an estimated cost of Rs 1 crore. The work was allotted at Rs 63.56 lakh, of which Rs 36.08 lakh has been utilised. The department said the work is 50 per cent physically complete. On the demand for construction and upgradation of sports infrastructure in Tral and other constituencies, the department said it had received a D.O. letter from MLA Rafiq Ahmad Naik dated February 23, 2026, regarding strengthening of sports infrastructure in the constituency. “The matter is under consideration in the Department,” the government said, adding that three works have been proposed for execution/construction under the appropriate schemes, subject to availability of funds and feasibility. The department further said it had received 183 demands from various constituencies and districts - 158 from the J&K Sports Council and 25 from the Directorate of Youth Services and Sports - submitted by public representatives, social activists and other stakeholders. Of these, 107 demands have been taken up for execution, while the remaining demands would be considered in a phased manner, subject to availability of free and encumbrance-free land, requisite funds and feasibility of the proposed works. On whether the government plans further upgradation of existing stadiums and development of new sports infrastructure in underserved and rural constituencies, particularly Tral, during the current financial year, the Minister said the department would consider such proposals. The provision of sports infrastructure in rural constituencies and underserved areas, including Tral, would be subject to availability of suitable land and funds, technical feasibility, approval under the relevant scheme and approval of the competent authority, the reply said.

The project received Rs 35 lakh, Rs 41.95 lakh and Rs 9.35 lakh during 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 respectively, with utilisation of Rs 3.96 lakh, Rs 37.39 lakh and Rs 7.95 lakh.
A second project for development of a playfield at Koil Shikargah was sanctioned during 2025-26 at an estimated cost of Rs 1 crore.
The department said the work is 50 per cent physically complete.

On the demand for construction and upgradation of sports infrastructure in Tral and other constituencies, the department said it had received a D.O. letter from MLA Rafiq Ahmad Naik dated February 23, 2026, regarding strengthening of sports infrastructure in the constituency.

“The matter is under consideration in the Department,” the government said, adding that three works have been proposed for execution/construction under the appropriate schemes, subject to availability of funds and feasibility.

The department further said it had received 183 demands from various constituencies and districts - 158 from the J&K Sports Council and 25 from the Directorate of Youth Services and Sports - submitted by public representatives, social activists and other stakeholders.

Of these, 107 demands have been taken up for execution, while the remaining demands would be considered in a phased manner, subject to availability of free and encumbrance-free land, requisite funds and feasibility of the proposed works.

On whether the government plans further upgradation of existing stadiums and development of new sports infrastructure in underserved and rural constituencies, particularly Tral, during the current financial year, the Minister said the department would consider such proposals.

The provision of sports infrastructure in rural constituencies and underserved areas, including Tral, would be subject to availability of suitable land and funds, technical feasibility, approval under the relevant scheme and approval of the competent authority, the reply said.

stories.headline: India raises concerns over US Russia sanctions law
stories.title: India raises concerns over US Russia sanctions law
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, during his meeting with a bipartisan US Congressional delegation, conveyed India's "concerns" over the implications of the recently enacted Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA) on bilateral ties and the international energy market, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday.

The meeting took place in Delhi on Sunday, and the US delegation was led by Brian Mast, Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to a query at his bi-weekly media briefing.
"Various issues of bilateral nature were discussed at the meeting.

Also, the foreign secretary conveyed our concerns about the SRIA legislation, as to the kind of implications it would have for bilateral relationships, as well as for the international energy market," Jaiswal said.

US President Donald Trump recently signed into law the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including China and India.

In response to a query on the next India-Russia summit, and if there was any timeline for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Russia to attend it, Jaiswal said, "The last annual summit with Russia was held in India, and we were delighted to host President (Vladimir) Putin.
The next meeting will be held in Russia, and we are still some distance away from it.
We'll keep you updated with the details in that regard."
At the invitation of Modi, Putin paid a state visit to India from December 4-5, 2025, for the 23rd India-Russia annual summit.
Ahead of the summit, the MEA had said that it would set the vision for strengthening the India-Russia 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'.

stories.headline: Statehood vs Panchayat polls : ‘Appropriate time’: CM Omar’s retort to BJP
stories.title: Statehood vs Panchayat polls : ‘Appropriate time’: CM Omar’s retort to BJP
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 29: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday turned the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) repeated “appropriate time” response on restoration of statehood against the party in the Legislative Assembly, saying his government could use the same phrase when asked about the timeline for Panchayat elections in Jammu & Kashmir. Responding to a question by BJP MLA R S Pathania on when the Panchayat elections would be held, Omar drew a parallel with the Centre’s position on statehood, saying, “You say appropriate time for statehood, we will say the same for Panchayat polls.” The Chief Minister added that if the BJP continued to seek clarity on the schedule for Panchayat elections, the government could similarly respond that the polls would be held at an “appropriate time”. He questioned the ambiguity surrounding the phrase, pointing out that the BJP had repeatedly invoked an appropriate time for restoring statehood without specifying when that time would arrive or how it would be determined. The exchange came amid the continuing political confrontation between the National Conference-led government and the BJP over the restoration of J&K’s statehood, with Omar using the issue to question the Opposition’s demand for a definite timeline on local body elections. Pertinently, the grassroots institutions remain without elected representatives. The issue assumes significance as J&K continues to remain without elected representatives across all three tiers of its Panchayati Raj system. The terms of Halqa Panchayats and Block Development Councils (BDCs) expired on January 9, 2024, while the tenure of District Development Councils (DDCs) ended in February 2026. Consequently, all three tiers of elected rural local governance are currently without elected representatives. The delay has left grassroots governance dependent on administrative arrangements, with Block Development Officers having been appointed as administrators following the expiry of the Panchayat and BDC terms. The government informed the Assembly last week that no specific timeline could be indicated for the Panchayat elections, stating that preparatory work was under way and that the statutory authority to conduct and schedule the polls rested with the State Election Commission. The election preparations involve revision of electoral rolls, delimitation and reservation-related exercises. The process has also been linked to the implementation of Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservation following amendments to local body laws in February 2024. A Dedicated Backward Classes Commission, constituted in June 2024, submitted its final report on February 27, 2025. However, the reservation framework and related procedural requirements remain central to preparations for the polls. The State Election Commission initiated the revision of Panchayat electoral rolls in March 2026, fixing April 1 as the qualifying date. The exercise formed part of the preparatory process for the next round of local body elections. The delay has also prolonged the absence of elected representatives at the village, block and district levels, institutions that play a key role in local development planning and the implementation of government schemes. Omar’s remarks on Tuesday brought the unresolved question of Panchayat elections into the wider political debate over statehood, with the Chief Minister challenging the BJP to explain why a definite timeline should be expected for local polls when the Centre has not provided one for restoring Jammu and Kashmir’s full statehood. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters, LoP Sunil Sharma said the Chief Minister is duty-bound to hold Panchayat Polls. “It’s the people who will ask him when he will hold elections. Let Omar go to any Panchayat Halqa he will face the music,” LoP claimed.
